Raised to P1: LevelDB abort when a cursor outlives ResizeCache is a node crash reachable from normal RPC use; sits with the other crash fixes.
Raised to P1: out-of-bounds reads in the UniValue tokenizer are a memory-safety defect in a vendored parsing primitive, ranking with the other correctness/safety fixes.

inconsistencies: Three PRs solve the same trace-logging problem: #34038 (-trace replacing -loglevel), #35387 (-loglevel enabling categories plus a loglevel RPC) and #35355 (-trace plus atomics). Review #34038 first as the design decision; #35387 and #35355 should be judged against it rather than in parallel.

#35322 and #35355 both replace the Logger category map/global level with atomic bitmasks; they duplicate each other's core change and must not be merged independently. #34730 is explicitly blocked on the #34038 outcome.

Settings/args chain, review in this order: #16545 -> #17580 -> {#17783, #17493} -> #17581. #31260 claims to be the foundation for runtime type checking in #16545 while #16545 claims to unblock the rest; the direction between #31260 and #16545 is circular as described and should be clarified before either is reviewed in depth.
util::Result chain: #25665 first, then #26022, then #25722; #29700 is also based on #25665. Reviewing #25722 or #29700 before #25665 wastes effort.

#36417 fixes a defect in the BIP352 input-key extraction added by #32966, which is itself unmerged. The two should be reviewed together, #32966 first; #36417 has no standalone value until the base lands.
#36190 is a functional test for the Windows wrapper behavior implemented in #36105; the test cannot be evaluated or merged before the runtime fix.
#36443 depends on #36442; #35558 is stacked on #35724 (outside this category); #19460 depends on #10102 and #29409 and is really multiprocess work that only touches utils incidentally.
#29256 scored higher alone than #34778, which it declares as its base; the prerequisite was raised so it no longer sits below the work it unblocks.
#35688 and #35818 both fix undefined behavior that is only reachable from test and fuzz harnesses; they were scored eleven positions apart despite being the same kind of fix.
result.notes: No PR in this category had been given P1 on its own, yet four of them are node crashes or data destruction in shared primitives (#35524, #36049, #35744, #35281) and are clearly more consequential than the rest; the band was opened for them so the config/perf/refactor P2s are not read as equally urgent. The large P2 block is mostly the argument-handling and util::Result foundation chains, which are ordered by dependency rather than by solo score, so several PRs that scored highly alone (#17783, #25665) now appear behind their prerequisites or behind user-visible fixes.
